role.altitude: The door mechanic keeps measuring and judging openings, identifying parts, explaining bills and talking with customers; filling paper work orders, looking up parts by phone, checking space tables and writing receipts shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the mobile work order and catalogue on site
role.ambitious_version: A mechanic whose work order, order and invoice are done when they leave the site.

tasks.short: Record work done, fault and cause, parts and hours, note recommendations, get the customer's signature, and hand in the work order to complete required paperwork.

steps.what: Door mechanic records the work done, the fault and the cause on the work order

loop.input: The mechanic's voice note at the door.
loop.output: Draft work text and a suggested fault and cause code from the company's lists.
loop.check: The code must exist in the company's fault list; the mechanic confirms or picks another.
loop.stop: No matching code goes to the planner; the mechanic types the text when the draft is wrong.
loop.why_not_simpler: Mechanics describe the same fault in many ways.

steps.what: Door mechanic records parts used and hours worked
Door mechanic notes recommended further work
Door mechanic goes through the work order with the customer and gets their signature
Door mechanic hands in the paper work orders at the office

tasks.design: A mobile work order replaces the paper form. The mechanic speaks a short voice note at the door; the app drafts the work text and suggests a fault and cause code from the company's list, and the mechanic confirms or picks another. Parts are scanned from the van stock, and hours come from starting and stopping the job. Recommendations are picked from a list with room for a remark. The customer signs on the phone and the work order syncs to the office, so nothing is handed in. Time stamps are used for invoicing, and any other use is agreed with the works council first.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper forms were filled by hand and retyped by the office.
tasks.enabler_now: Mobile work orders with voice notes, fault lists and parts scanning.
tasks.still_hard: Mechanics who prefer writing to speaking.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining to the customer why the old spring broke.

ambition.what: See which door models fail most from fault codes.

tasks.altitude: Much less paperwork; the customer conversation stays.

reach.learn: Whether invoices go out the same day.

evidence.claim: A work order product for installers and door companies runs from quote to invoice.
Voice memos are transcribed into the work order.
A fibre network firm reported about 8 hours per technician per week saved on work-order mail, entry and reports; vendor case, period not stated.
Work orders with time stamps can observe technicians and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: completing paperwork; ordering parts (task 8404) and collecting payment (task 8390) are sibling tasks.
Input contract for s2: van stock with barcodes kept by the warehouse; parts not on the van are typed.
The signature conversation keeps its full time.
unknowns: Share of mechanics using voice notes.
research_questions: Are work orders complete without office follow-up?

already_counted.description: Door mechanic corrects drafted work text and codes.

incremental.description: Door mechanic reports missing fault codes and van stock barcodes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: mechanics typing instead of speaking and partial barcodes; high: full use of voice notes, scanning and sync.

tasks.short: Identify the needed spring, section or slat, look it up in supplier catalogues, check the final order, order replacement springs, sections or slats, and follow up delivery.

steps.what: Door mechanic identifies the needed spring, section or slat: door model, spring size and section dimensions
Door mechanic looks up the part in supplier catalogues

loop.input: The mechanic's description and measurements of the part.
loop.output: Candidate lines from the supplier catalogue in the work order app.
loop.check: Wire size, length, inside diameter or section dimensions must match the measurements exactly.
loop.stop: No exact match: the mechanic calls the supplier.
loop.why_not_simpler: Mechanics describe parts in their own words and catalogues name them differently.

steps.what: Door mechanic checks the final order: part, quantity, price and delivery address
Door mechanic orders the replacement springs, sections or slats from the supplier
Door mechanic follows up delivery and plans the return visit

approvals.approved_version: The order lines, quantities, prices and delivery address as checked by the mechanic in s3; any change needs a new check before ordering.

tasks.design: Identifying the part stays with the mechanic at the door. The supplier catalogue is loaded in the work order app, and a matching step proposes catalogue lines from the mechanic's description and measurements; only exact matches on size are shown. The mechanic checks the order and sends that version electronically to the supplier from the work order, instead of phoning. Delivery status appears on the work order, so the return visit is planned without calling the supplier.
tasks.previous_blocker: Parts were ordered by phone from paper catalogues.
tasks.enabler_now: Supplier catalogues and electronic ordering linked to mobile work orders.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising an old door model from its hardware.

evidence.claim: A work order product for installers and door companies runs from quote to invoice.
Matching free-text parts to catalogue lines works as a bounded step with a person approving.

assumptions: Boundary: ordering parts; completing work orders (task 8391) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s2 and s4: the main suppliers' catalogues and ordering linked to the work order app, about 75% of parts; s2 and s4 are priced at that share.
Identifying and checking keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of parts from linked suppliers.

incremental.description: Door mechanic reports catalogue lines that do not match real parts.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many old doors and small suppliers; high: most parts from linked suppliers.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Measure the opening, assess headroom, side room and wall, ceiling and power conditions, check measurements against door types, determine appropriateness of the door for the location, and record findings for the quote.

steps.what: Door mechanic measures the opening, headroom, side room and backroom
Door mechanic inspects the job site: wall, ceiling, floor and power supply conditions
Door mechanic checks the measurements against each door type's space requirements
Door mechanic determines the appropriate door for the location
Door mechanic records measurements, photos and findings for the quote

tasks.design: Measuring and inspecting stay hands-on. The mechanic enters the measurements in a site survey form in the work order app, which checks them against the minimum headroom, side room and backroom of each door type and track option and shows which fit, instead of the mechanic looking them up in printed tables. Choosing the door stays with the mechanic. Photos and findings go into the same form and feed the quote.
tasks.previous_blocker: Space requirements sat in printed tables and notes were on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Site survey forms with door specification rules.
tasks.still_hard: Openings with beams, pipes or uneven floors.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing that the lintel will not carry the door.
tasks.altitude: Less looking up; judging the site stays.

reach.learn: Whether quotes need fewer follow-up questions.

evidence.claim: Load and space computations work as deterministic calculators.

assumptions: Boundary: inspecting sites; studying blueprints for opener installation (task 8402) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s3: space requirements per door type entered from the manufacturers' specifications by the office.
Measuring, inspecting and choosing keep their full time.
research_questions: Do doors that do not fit at installation fall?

incremental.description: Door mechanic reports specification changes for new door types.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: unusual openings; high: standard garage doors.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Compute the amount from parts and hours, explain the bill, collect payment upon job completion, record the payment, and follow up unpaid jobs.

steps.what: Door mechanic computes the amount from parts, hours and the price list
Door mechanic explains the bill to the customer
Door mechanic collects payment by card or cash
Door mechanic writes the receipt and records the payment for the office
Door mechanic follows up customers who did not pay on site

tasks.design: The work order app prices parts and hours from the price list, so the mechanic checks a total instead of calculating it. Explaining the bill stays personal. A mobile card terminal linked to the work order takes the amount without retyping, and the payment and receipt are recorded in the work order and accounting, instead of a paper receipt and cash slips handed to the office. Following up unpaid jobs stays a personal call.
tasks.previous_blocker: Amounts were calculated by hand and payments recorded on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Work orders priced from the price list and card terminals linked to them.
tasks.human_edge: Settling a disagreement about the bill on the doorstep.
tasks.altitude: Less arithmetic and paper; the customer talk stays.

reach.learn: Whether site payments match invoices without follow-up.

evidence.claim: A work order product for installers and door companies runs from quote to invoice with accounting links.

assumptions: Boundary: collecting payment; completing work orders (task 8391) is a sibling task.
Input contract for s1: parts and hours recorded on the work order under task 8391 and the price list kept by the office.
Explaining and following up keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of jobs paid on site.

incremental.description: Door mechanic reports price list errors.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many cash payments; high: card payments linked to the work order.
